runes.name: Thrice
runes.text: The spell flies three times in a fan, each at 40% of its damage; only the middle one carries its statuses
runes.lore: The Wardens cut this rune into the bolts of their crossbows, so that a guard who missed the first time would not miss the third.

runes.name: Reprise
runes.text: Half a second later the spell comes again at half its damage and statuses
runes.lore: Spoken twice, a word carries twice as far. The chapel's choir sang every verse once more, softer, for those still on the stair.

runes.name: Seeking
runes.text: Its bolts curve towards foes; its hands reach further and rise under the foe nearest your aim
runes.lore: A pilgrim lost in the crypts followed this rune scratched on the walls. It never led to the way out, only to whatever waited.

runes.name: Wide
runes.text: Its ring, ground, wall or circle is half again as large, and strikes 20% less hard
runes.lore: The sextons chalked it round the ossuary's doors, so the warding reached the whole stair and not only the step they stood on.

runes.name: Quicken
runes.text: Ready again 30% sooner, for 20% more mana
runes.lore: Hurried magic is dearer magic. The apprentices who carved it learned that quickly, and the ones who didn't learned it once.

runes.name: Vein
runes.text: Short of mana, it takes what mana you have and half a heart for the rest (never your last)
runes.lore: The embalmers wrote in blood when their ink ran dry. Their ledgers are still legible; the embalmers are not.

runes.name: Lasting
runes.text: What the spell leaves lasts half again as long (its ground, wall, mantle, motes, hold or mark), for 20% more mana
runes.lore: Candles in the reliquary burned for a week on a finger of wax. The sextons swore by this rune, and never told the pilgrims why.
